title: Localize the boundary form before taking an energy estimate
reviewed_arguments: All 17 original obligations, all 18 labelled displays and all three complete solutions are retained unchanged.

The intrinsic weak-derivative H1 space equals the exact restricted Sobolev space: tangential zero extension and the distributional Fourier identity give the tangential norm, and the complete earlier normal-step theorem supplies both norm bounds and completeness.
The actual L2 adjoint follows by approximation in both slots using the order-zero bounds. Uniqueness and the equivalent H1 norm are explicit.

Both the localizer and its adjoint preserve the Dirichlet form domain by all-zero boundary jets, zero extension, translation, supported mollification and large cutoffs. Their H1 bounds preserve the Neumann form domain without a false strong derivative condition.
The compressed normal commutator includes the lower-order symbol followed by the normal derivative. Every commutator extends H1 to L2 by the exact density and symbol bounds.
Every ordered principal, complex first-order and zeroth-order defect term is proved by the L2 adjoint identity. The source is an antilinear functional on the actual test domain.
All coefficient norm sums, source dual bounds and the factor one over four epsilon are retained. The proof makes no coercivity or uniform shrinking-window claim.
Uniform families require common finite symbol seminorms, including the adjoint and differentiated symbols; individually order-zero operators do not establish that hypothesis.
The real multiplication example has the exact nonzero defect; the complex version is qualified by its real part. The Neumann example has the positive boundary contribution with the exact sign.

The tent function belongs to the Dirichlet space by zero extension and approximation. Its source has weights plus two and minus one, bounded point evaluations follow from FTC and Cauchy-Schwarz, and shrinking bumps rule out an L2 representative.
The new coordinate figure depicts the exact graph and interior source weights. Its arrows are not a density and no whole-line zero-extension source is inferred.
Vasy Section 4, PDF 23–26, was read with the distinct half-order and epsilon source hypotheses. The external microlocal estimates are later obligations, not imported programme proofs.
